chunks: And Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Walīd, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:

Four things go to waste: affection granted to one who has no loyalty, a favor placed with one who does not appreciate it, knowledge taught to one who does not listen to it, and a secret entrusted to one who has no safeguarding of it.

key_terms.حَضَانَةَ: Protective keeping or safeguarding of what is entrusted
key_terms.سِرٌّ: A private matter or confidential secret
key_terms.عِلْمٌ: Knowledge that is taught and conveyed
key_terms.مَعْرُوفٌ: A good deed, kindness, or favor done for someone
key_terms.مَوَدَّةٌ: Affection or loving regard shown to another
key_terms.وَفَاءَ: Loyalty and faithfulness in a relationship

ai.seo_question: What four things does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say are wasted when given to the wrong people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches that some noble things are lost when placed with those unfit to receive them. The hadith stresses discernment in affection, beneficence, teaching, and entrusting private matters, highlighting loyalty, gratitude, receptivity, and trustworthiness as essential moral qualities.
